overall: Atlanta is under an active Heat Advisory through 8PM EDT with heat index values up to 106°F, indicating a very hot and humid day. No current observations are available (temp/dewpoint sensors not yet reporting), but the atmospheric setup — residual overnight warmth with a low near 77°F and light winds — is consistent with an aggressive heating day. Afternoon storm chances (30% after 2PM) are unlikely to limit the daily high, which is typically achieved before convection initiates.
forecast_obs_notes: Model guidance is notably spread: GFS is a clear warm outlier at 96.7°F, while ECMWF (94.6°F), HRRR (93.1°F), and NBM (92.9°F) cluster 2-4 degrees cooler. The NWS official forecast of 94°F aligns closely with the ECMWF and sits above the HRRR/NBM cluster. The even-bucket ensemble identifies 96-97°F as the top bucket at 16.9%, driven largely by GFS weight, but the odd-bucket top of 91-92°F at 21.1% with an 'Avoid' tier signal reflects substantial distributional uncertainty.
max_temp_prediction: The most defensible estimate anchors near the NWS official forecast and ECMWF consensus around 94-95°F. The GFS at 96.7°F appears to be an upside outlier; three of the four models sit at or below 94.6°F. For the active even-bucket market, the top bucket of 96-97°F carries the highest single probability (16.9%) but is buoyed by a bullish GFS; the 94-95°F bucket at just 0.5% seems underweighted relative to the NWS/multi-model consensus, suggesting market model calibration may be skewed hot. Confidence is moderate-low given absent observational data and the Tier 3/Tier 4 ensemble signals.
